These feelings really started building not long after I took on some extra STEM teaching and club responsibilities at my school.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities over the past year and a half, or has it been a persistent low mood?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had any periods where things got better. It has been a very persistent, heavy feeling that has just steadily built up and stayed constant the entire time. I haven't had any breaks from this joyless state since it started.\n\nDoctor: Do you often feel guilty or worthless about your situation or performance as a teacher, or is it more about just not feeling any pleasure or interest in things?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it is very much both. I feel a deep sense of guilt and constantly spiral into thinking I'm a terrible teacher and wife who is letting everyone down when minor things go wrong. At the same time, I feel completely flat even when a lesson goes well, and I've lost all interest in teaching and my usual hobbies like softball and hiking.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about your energy levels and motivation? Have you noticed any changes in your ability to initiate or complete tasks, or do you feel fatigued most of the time?\n\nPatient: I feel completely exhausted all the time, and coming home from school leaves me so drained that simple chores like folding laundry feel like climbing a mountain. At night, my mind spins with school worries for hours before I can fall asleep, and then I wake up around 4 or 5 a.m. unable to get back to sleep.\n\nDoctor: You've been experiencing these symptoms for about a year and a half, but can you tell me if there was a specific event or period that triggered the onset of these feelings, or did they gradually build up over time?\n\nPatient: They definitely built up gradually, but it all started about two years ago when I took on a lot of extra responsibilities like the advanced STEM track, test prep, and running two clubs. Around that same time, our district introduced a demanding new evaluation system, and the pressure and joylessness just steadily worsened over the next 18 months.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any previous episodes of depression or significant low mood before this 1.5-year period, or is this the first time you've felt this way?\n\nPatient: This is the very first time I've ever felt this way. I have no prior history of depression or anything like this before this period started.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've been experiencing these symptoms for about a year and a half without any significant improvement, and considering this is your first episode, do you think the pressures and stressors from your job and personal life have been consistently present and unrelenting over this entire period?\n\nPatient: Yes, the pressures have been absolutely unrelenting and constant the entire time. It has just been a non-stop cycle that matches exactly how long I've been feeling this way.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes where you heard voices, saw things that weren't there, or had thoughts that didn't seem like your own during this 1.5-year period?\n\nPatient: No, nothing like that has ever happened to me. I haven't had any breaks from this joyless state since it started.\n\nDoctor: Do you often feel guilty or worthless about your situation or performance as a teacher, or is it more about just not feeling any pleasure or interest in things?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it is very much both. It is more of a heavy, self-critical loop than anything unusual.\n\nDoctor: You've denied having any hallucinations or delusions, but can you confirm whether you've experienced any significant disorganization in your thoughts or behaviors that might seem out of character or hard to explain to others?\n\nPatient: While I don't have any bizarre or unexplainable behaviors in a psychotic sense, I have experienced a severe and completely out-of-character decline in my ability to stay organized. My brain feels so foggy that I struggle with simple decisions and grading, and my once meticulous home routines and finances have fallen into complete disarray. I just feel too overwhelmed and drained to manage any of it anymore.\n\nDoctor: You've had a persistent low mood for about a year and a half without significant improvement, but can you tell me if there were any distinct periods within this time frame where your symptoms seemed to worsen or if it has been a steady, unchanging state?\n\nPatient: It has been more of a steady, gradual decline rather than coming and going in distinct waves. Right now, I am just trying to survive the overwhelming feelings of my present situation. It is really hard to look ahead when just getting through each day takes everything I have.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling exhausted and having trouble initiating tasks, can you tell me if you've also experienced any physical slowing down, such as slowed speech or movements, over the past year and a half?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed any physical slowing down or changes in my speech or movements. Even on days when a lesson goes really well or the kids in the robotics club do something clever, I still just feel flat and can't experience any real lift in my mood.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've had this persistent low mood for a year and a half without any significant improvement, and this is your first episode, do you think it's possible that you might experience another episode like this in the future, or do you feel like the circumstances that led to this episode are unique and unlikely to recur?\n\nPatient: To be honest, I haven't thought much about the future or whether this could happen again. Because this heavy, flat feeling is so constant now—even on days when things go well at school—it's hard for me to imagine feeling better just by reducing my workload. I don't know for sure, though.\n\nDoctor: Can you elaborate on how your feelings of guilt and worthlessness affect your daily life and interactions with others, such as your students, colleagues, and family members?\n\nPatient: Whenever a student's scores dip or I miss a deadline, I spiral into thinking I'm a terrible teacher and a bad wife who is letting everyone down. I constantly replay my past mistakes, feeling like I don't even deserve my job or my husband's support. It makes me withdraw from everyone, which has only created more tension at home.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide, or have you ever wished you wouldn't wake up, as a way to escape these feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and constant pressure?\n\nPatient: Yes, especially at night when I'm lying awake feeling like I'm failing at everything, I do catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up or got into some kind of accident.
